taxonomy.note: Current Kew accepts the species with three subspecies. The learner stays at species rank because Hays/Travis/Williamson records span differing subspecific treatments.

evidence: Hays — project Master Plant Pool flags Sideroxylon lanuginosum as Hays-local with 17 wild observations.
Travis — UT Plant Resources Center herbarium index includes Sideroxylon lanuginosum var. albicans from Travis County; modern treatments place the local complex within S. lanuginosum.
Williamson — UT Plant Resources Center provides a detailed county treatment of Sideroxylon lanuginosum subsp. oblongifolium.
target_zone_range.guardrail: Species-level PASS is used because current Kew accepts multiple infraspecific taxa under S. lanuginosum and local Central Texas records have historically shifted among those ranks.

morphology.look_here_first: Start with the twig tips and leaf underside. Gum bumelia is a shrub or small tree with some short shoots ending in sharp spine-like tips, simple entire leaves, and young foliage that is distinctly woolly or tawny beneath. Older leaves become glossier above while the lower surface stays conspicuously hairy.
diagnostic_traits: some short shoots terminate in sharp spine-like tips
young lower leaf surface woolly/tomentose, often tawny
older upper leaf surface glossier and less hairy
small flowers in fascicles from short shoots

confusers.separator: Confirm the combination of alternate entire leaves, woolly/tawny leaf undersides, and spine-like short shoots rather than relying on thorns alone.
